\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಶ್ಲಾಘಿಸು} (ślāghisu)}{ಶ್ಲಾಘಿಸು (ślāghisu)}]{\kn{ಶ್ಲಾಘಿಸು} (ślāghisu) — to commend}

\label{lesson:KA-C389-slaghisu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for well-being, then the Kannada for to condemn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಶ್ಲಾಘಿಸು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಶ್ಲಾಘಿಸು}} — \emph{ślāghisu} — \textquotedblleft{}to commend\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಊರಿನ} \kn{ಜನರು} \kn{ಆ} \kn{ಹುಡುಗನ} \kn{ಧೈರ್ಯವನ್ನು} \kn{ಶ್ಲಾಘಿಸಿದರು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ūrina janaru ā huḍugana dhairyavannu ślāghisidaru.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The villagers commended the boy's courage.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ಶ್ಲಾಘಿಸಿದೆ}, \emph{ślāghiside}.

What is commended takes -\kn{ಅನ್ನು}. \kn{ಶ್ಲಾಘನೀಯ}, praiseworthy.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಶ್ಲಾಘಿಸು}} (\emph{ślāghisu}) is built on Sanskrit \emph{ślāghā}, \textquotedblleft{}boasting; praise\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12736), with the Kannada verb ending -\emph{isu}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ślāghisu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ślāghisu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ūrina janaru ā huḍugana dhairyavannu ślāghisidaru.} — The villagers commended the boy's courage.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for well-being, then the Kannada for to condemn, then say \emph{ślāghisu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಶ್ಲಾಘಿಸು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To commend\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಪುರಸ್ಕರಿಸು} (puraskarisu)}{ಪುರಸ್ಕರಿಸು (puraskarisu)}]{\kn{ಪುರಸ್ಕರಿಸು} (puraskarisu) — to felicitate; to honour}

\label{lesson:KA-C389-puraskarisu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to condemn, then the Kannada for to commend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಪುರಸ್ಕರಿಸು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಪುರಸ್ಕರಿಸು}} — \emph{puraskarisu} — \textquotedblleft{}to felicitate; to honour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಶಾಲೆ} \kn{ಉತ್ತಮ} \kn{ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳನ್ನು} \kn{ಪುರಸ್ಕರಿಸಿತು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{śāle uttama vidyārthigaḷannu puraskarisitu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The school honoured its best students.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ಪುರಸ್ಕರಿಸಿದೆ}, \emph{puraskariside}.

\kn{ಪುರಸ್ಕಾರ}, an honour or an award.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಪುರಸ್ಕರಿಸು}} (\emph{puraskarisu}) is built on Sanskrit \emph{puraskāra}, \textquotedblleft{}placing in front, honouring\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the Kannada verb ending -\emph{isu}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{puraskarisu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{puraskarisu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śāle uttama vidyārthigaḷannu puraskarisitu.} — The school honoured its best students.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to condemn, then the Kannada for to commend, then say \emph{puraskarisu} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠೆ} (pratiṣṭhe)}{ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠೆ (pratiṣṭhe)}]{\kn{ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠೆ} (pratiṣṭhe) — prestige}

\label{lesson:KA-C389-pratisthe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to commend, then the Kannada for to felicitate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠೆ}} — \emph{pratiṣṭhe} — \textquotedblleft{}prestige\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಈ} \kn{ಗೆಲುವು} \kn{ನಮ್ಮ} \kn{ಊರಿನ} \kn{ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠೆಯ} \kn{ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ī geluvu namma ūrina pratiṣṭheya praśne.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This win is a matter of our town's prestige.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತ}, prestigious.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠೆ}} (\emph{pratiṣṭhe}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{pratiṣṭhā}, \textquotedblleft{}a foundation, a firm standing\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8608).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pratiṣṭhe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pratiṣṭhe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ī geluvu namma ūrina pratiṣṭheya praśne.} — This win is a matter of our town's prestige.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to commend, then the Kannada for to felicitate, then say \emph{pratiṣṭhe} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಉತ್ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಿಸು} (utprēkṣisu)}{ಉತ್ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಿಸು (utprēkṣisu)}]{\kn{ಉತ್ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಿಸು} (utprēkṣisu) — to exaggerate}

\label{lesson:KA-C389-utpreksisu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to felicitate, then the Kannada for prestige.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಉತ್ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಿಸು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಉತ್ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಿಸು}} — \emph{utprēkṣisu} — \textquotedblleft{}to exaggerate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಅವನು} \kn{ತನ್ನ} \kn{ಸಾಹಸವನ್ನು} \kn{ಉತ್ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಿಸಿದನು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avanu tanna sāhasavannu utprēkṣisidanu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He exaggerated his exploit.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ಉತ್ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಿಸಿದೆ}, \emph{utprēkṣiside}.

\kn{ಉತ್ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷೆ}, an exaggeration.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಉತ್ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಿಸು}} (\emph{utprēkṣisu}) is built on Sanskrit \emph{utprekṣā}, which in poetics names a fanciful comparison (Monier-Williams), with the Kannada verb ending -\emph{isu}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to felicitate, then the Kannada for prestige, then say \emph{utprēkṣisu} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಸ್ಥಾನಮಾನ} (sthānamāna)}{ಸ್ಥಾನಮಾನ (sthānamāna)}]{\kn{ಸ್ಥಾನಮಾನ} (sthānamāna) — status; standing}

\label{lesson:KA-C389-sthanamana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for prestige, then the Kannada for to exaggerate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸ್ಥಾನಮಾನ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸ್ಥಾನಮಾನ}} — \emph{sthānamāna} — \textquotedblleft{}status; standing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಊರಿನಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಅವರಿಗೆ} \kn{ಒಳ್ಳೆಯ} \kn{ಸ್ಥಾನಮಾನ} \kn{ಇದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ūrinalli avarige oḷḷeya sthānamāna ide.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They have a good standing in the town.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಸ್ಥಾನ} (place) + \kn{ಮಾನ} (honour).

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಸ್ಥಾನಮಾನ}} (\emph{sthānamāna}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{sthāna}, \textquotedblleft{}a place, a position\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13753), paired with \emph{māna}, \textquotedblleft{}honour, respect\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sthānamāna}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ūrinalli avarige oḷḷeya sthānamāna ide.} — They have a good standing in the town.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for prestige, then the Kannada for to exaggerate, then say \emph{sthānamāna} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
